learn.title: Sorting triangles
learn.body: A triangle has three sides and three angles. We sort triangles in two ways: by how many sides are equal, and by the size of the biggest angle. The names tell you what to expect before you measure anything.

learn.title: By sides
learn.body: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides. An isosceles triangle has at least two equal sides. A scalene triangle has no equal sides. So an equilateral triangle is also isosceles, but not the other way round.

learn.title: By angles
learn.body: An acute triangle has three acute angles. A right triangle has one right angle. An obtuse triangle has one obtuse angle. A triangle can never have more than one right or obtuse angle, because the three angles must fit in $180^\circ$.

learn.title: Can these sides form a triangle?
learn.body: The sum of any two sides must be greater than the third side.
steps: Try $3,4,8$: $3+4=7$, which is not greater than 8.
With sides 5 and 9, the third side is between $9-5=4$ and $9+5=14$.

learn.body: The longest side is always opposite the largest angle, and the shortest side is opposite the smallest.

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides $5,5,8$. What is it?
questions.explanation: Two sides are equal, and not all three, so it is isosceles.

questions.prompt: A triangle has angles $40^\circ,60^\circ,80^\circ$. How do you classify it by angles?
questions.explanation: All three angles are under $90^\circ$, so it is acute. (They add to $180^\circ$.)

questions.prompt: Which three lengths can form a triangle?
questions.explanation: $4+5=9>8$ works. In the others the two shorter sides do not add to more than the longest.

questions.prompt: A triangle with no equal sides is \_\_.
questions.explanation: Scalene means all three sides have different lengths.

questions.prompt: Two sides of a triangle are 5 and 9. What is the largest whole number the third side can be?
questions.explanation: The third side must be less than $5+9=14$, so the largest whole number is 13.

questions.prompt: Is every equilateral triangle also isosceles?
choices: Yes, it has at least two equal sides
Only if it is a right triangle
questions.explanation: Isosceles means at least two equal sides, and an equilateral triangle has three.

questions.prompt: Match each triangle to its description.
questions.explanation: The first two names sort by sides, the last two by angles.
